title: centaurea stoebe subsp. australis
intro: Centaurea stoebe subsp. australis, commonly known as the South Australian knawel, is a subspecies of flowering plant in the knapweed family (Asteraceae). It is a herbaceous perennial with a history of traditional use in folk medicine, particularly for its purported health benefits. The bioactive constituents of Centaurea stoebe subsp. australis are thought to include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and terpenoids, which are believed to provide therapeutic actions such as anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects. While the health benefits and therapeutic actions of Centaurea stoebe subsp. australis are not well-studied, it may offer potential benefits for inflammation, oxidative stress, and other conditions, although more research is needed to confirm its efficacy.
